title: Independent Director
description:
**The mandate through a project’s life** 




  





 The company designs and manufactures process equipment used in food\-production environments. The Board needs an Independent Director who can govern the entire obligation created when an engineered system is sold—from interpretation of process requirements through fabrication, site integration, performance acceptance and long\-term service. Success cannot be measured only by dispatch: an apparently complete project can still carry unresolved hygiene, performance, documentation or margin exposure.
 



  





**Gate one: accepting the problem** 




  





 Before a bid becomes a contract, management must understand the customer’s product, process conditions, cleaning method, utilities, interfaces, throughput assumptions and acceptance criteria. The Director will challenge bid governance where requirements are incomplete, guarantees are broad or the proposed solution relies on untested assumptions. Commercial urgency should not bypass engineering review, capacity confirmation, site\-risk assessment or a clear allocation of interface responsibility.
 



  





 The Board should receive visibility into contractual exposure for delay, performance shortfall, contamination, consequential loss, intellectual property and changes in customer scope. Risk premiums and contingencies must be grounded in the actual project rather than applied mechanically.
 



  





**Gate two: freezing a cleanable design** 




  





 The appointee will seek assurance that hygienic design principles are built into equipment geometry, material choice, seals, welds, drainage, accessibility, instrumentation and cleaning validation. Design review should involve manufacturing, quality, service and commissioning, not remain isolated within engineering.
 



  





 Changes after design freeze need controlled technical and commercial assessment.
 



  





 Where digital controls or remote connections form part of the system, the Board must understand software ownership, access privileges, patching, data use and safe fallback. A cyber event that changes a process parameter can become a product\-safety event.
 



  





**Gate three: fabricating what was approved** 




  





 Material identity, surface condition, welding practice, outsourced treatment, calibration and inspection evidence all influence fitness for use. The Director will review how the company qualifies special processes, controls non\-conformance and preserves traceability. Schedule pressure must not move unfinished or conditionally accepted work downstream without named accountability and an agreed closure path.
 



  





 Management information should connect shop loading, material availability, engineering releases, rework and subcontractor performance. Reported project progress should represent earned completion, not expenditure or physical presence on the shop floor.
 



  





**Gate four: integrating at site** 




  





 Installation and commissioning often expose assumptions that were invisible during design. The Director will question site\-readiness checks, change control, safety planning, customer dependencies and escalation routes. Acceptance tests should be objective, witnessed and tied to the contracted duty. Punch lists must distinguish cosmetic completion from issues that prevent safe or hygienic operation.
 



  





 Revenue recognition, retention, warranty provision and project closure should reflect substantive acceptance and remaining obligations. The finance view and the project view must reconcile.
 



  





**Gate five: learning through service** 




  





 Warranty calls, spares demand, cleaning difficulties and repeat interventions contain product\-development intelligence. The appointee will encourage a closed loop from service into design standards, supplier decisions and commercial qualification. Aftermarket strategy should create genuine availability and performance value, not dependency through inaccessible information or restrictive practices.
 



  





**The enterprise decisions surrounding the gates** 




  





 The Director will participate in capacity, technology and market choices. They will evaluate whether modularisation, standard platforms, automation or strategic sourcing can improve delivery without concealing customer\-specific engineering. Working\-capital oversight will cover advances, milestone billing, long\-lead purchases, work in progress, claims and retentions. The Board will expect candid scenario analysis before expanding facilities or entering unfamiliar applications.
 



  





 Leadership review will include engineering authority, project\-management capability, quality independence, service responsiveness and succession for scarce technical roles. Safety, environmental performance and contractor governance will be treated as operating fundamentals.
 



  





**Experience and temperament** 




  





 The ideal candidate has senior responsibility in process equipment, food manufacturing, capital projects, industrial engineering, quality, operations, finance or project\-based business. Experience governing hygienic design, complex commissioning, contract risk or lifecycle service will be useful. The Board needs a person who can explore a technical issue deeply while preserving the distinction between oversight and execution.
 



  





 Candidates must be financially literate, conflict\-free and actively registered in the IICA Independent Directors Databank. Any relationship with customers, engineering consultants, component suppliers, contractors or competing equipment businesses must be declared.
 



  





**Candidate response** 




  





 Applications through India ID Exchange should include the Board profile, IICA confirmation and a brief explanation of how the candidate would determine whether a delayed project is suffering from execution weakness, defective commercial assumptions or both.

* Proven experience as a Technical Lead in enterprise systems
* Strong experience in product development and modernization programs
* Solid understanding of Agile / Scrum methodologies

* Frontend: Angular, React
* Backend: Java, Spring Boot, REST APIs
* Databases: SQL Server, MongoDB

 Bachelors in Engineering or Masters in Computer Science or equivalent

* Entrepreneurial thinking and flexibility to change;
* Very good English communication skills (concise writing and orally convincing);
* Structured and clear writing skills;

 Eurofins Digital Testing offices are based in Bristol City Centre. We are right next to Cabot Circus and many bars and restaurants. Our office is easy to commute to and has fantastic views over the city centre too. This area is a great place to live and work, with lots going on.

* Good benefits and flexible working opportunities.
* Great location within the city centre.
* Opportunities to progress and grow with the company.

**Job summary**




  





 This job describes an integrated model covering planning, in\-house manufacturing and installation, and its case study specifically describes the project manager controlling installation against the approved floor plan, coordinating readiness, inspecting the completed installation with the client, and obtaining handover.
 



  





**Key Responsibilities:**




  




1. **Sales\-to\-Project Handover** 
 \- Take over confirmed PO, BOQ, quotation, approved drawings, specifications, finishes, and client commitments. Ensure complete and accurate project handover from Sales.
2. **Scope Validation** 
 \- Cross\-check PO, quotation, BOQ, and drawings. Identify and resolve quantity, specification, and scope discrepancies before execution.
3. **Project Kick\-Off** 
 \- Conduct project kick\-off meetings with Sales, Design, Engineering, Purchase, Maintenance, Production, QC, Logistics, Accounts and Installation teams. Define responsibilities, timelines, and deliverables.
4. **Project Planning \& Scheduling** 
 \- Prepare the master project schedule based on the committed delivery and handover date. Track project milestones and overall progress.
5. **Site Survey \& Verification** 
 \- Coordinate site measurements and verify site conditions, access, lift, loading, flooring, electrical, and other requirements. Ensure site readiness before execution.
6. **Drawing Coordination \& Approval** 
 \- Coordinate preparation and approval of GFC/AFC drawings. Ensure approved drawings are available before production.
7. **Engineering Release** 
 \- Coordinate detailed production drawings, BOMs, hardware, and special requirements. Ensure accurate and timely release of production information.
8. **Change \& Variation Management** 
 \- Control all changes and revisions through proper documentation and approvals. Evaluate impact on project cost, timeline, and resources.
9. **Material Readiness** 
 \- Monitor project\-specific and long\-lead materials with Purchase and Planning teams. Ensure materials are available as per the project schedule.
10. **Production Planning** 
 \- Coordinate production priorities based on project requirements and installation sequence. Ensure furniture is manufactured as per approved drawings and timelines.
11. **Production Monitoring** 
 \- Monitor planned versus actual production progress. Follow up with Production teams and resolve delays or bottlenecks.
12. **Quality Management** 
 \- Ensure pre\-dispatch inspection of dimensions, finishes, hardware, quantity, and functionality. Ensure products meet approved specifications and quality standards.
13. **Client \& Stakeholder Coordination** 
 \- Act as the primary project contact for clients, architects, PMCs, consultants, and contractors. Conduct regular project review meetings and maintain MOMs.
14. **Site Readiness Management** 
 \- Verify civil, flooring, painting, electrical, access, and other site requirements before dispatch. Confirm site readiness for installation.
15. **Dispatch \& Logistics Planning** 
 \- Plan floor\-wise/zone\-wise dispatch and delivery schedules. Coordinate packing, labeling, transportation, unloading, and material sequencing.
16. **Installation Planning** 
 \- Plan installation manpower, supervisors, tools, equipment, and work sequence. Set daily and weekly installation targets.
17. **Site Execution \& Monitoring** 
 \- Monitor daily installation activities and progress against approved drawings and schedules. Ensure installation quality, productivity, and safety requirements are maintained.
18. **Issue Resolution \& Escalation** 
 \- Identify and resolve shortages, damages, drawing mismatches, site obstructions, and other project issues. Track issues with responsible persons and target closure dates.
19. **Snag Management** 
 \- Conduct joint inspections with the client/PMC and prepare snag lists. Coordinate with concerned teams for timely snag closure.
20. **Project Handover \-** 
 Coordinate final inspection and completion of all pending works. Prepare handover documentation and obtain client sign\-off/handover certificate.
21. **Commercial Closure** 
 \- Support billing by providing dispatch, installation, handover, and approved variation documents. Coordinate closure of project\-related commercial requirements.
22. **Project Closure \& Review** 
 \- Review actual project performance against planned cost, timeline, quality, and resources. Document rework, shortages, delays, lessons learned, and project closure actions.
